text.p: A WebSecure Inc shareholder filed a class action lawsuit charging the company misled investors in its relationship to scandal-plagued Centennial Technologies Inc, his lawyer said Thursday.

Sanford Nager, who bought 2,000 shares of WebSecure at $8 each during its initial public offering in December, charged that investors were lured into buying the stock because of the company's affiliation with Centennial.
"Why would anyone invest in it other than the connection with Centennial?" Nager's lawyer Thomas Sanford told Reuters.
WebSecure declined to comment when contacted by Reuters.
Centennial fired Chief Executive Emanuel Pinez in February and later said it would have to restate its financial results for the last 3-1/2 years to report losses instead of profits.

When the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission charged Pinez inflated company sales, Centennial's and WebSecure's shares were battered. Pinez, held without bail on insider trading charges, has pled not guilty to the allegations.
Saugus, Mass.-based Websecure, which planned to offer Internet-related services and software, was trading at 3-15/16 in mid-afternoon trade on Friday, off from a high of $20 in early December.
Centennial, the best performing Big Board stock in 1996, has been delisted from the New York Stock Exchange.
The suit said alleged Centennial was one of WebSecure's customers, provided most of its financing, and was "critical to WebSecure's ability to complete a successful public offering of its stock."
The suit also charged that WebSecure had not fully revealed the value of two of its key software products.
"They did not disclose in the offering that they had already written off the software that they had acquired from two different companies," Shapiro said.

Named in the lawsuit are Centennial, WebSecure and four of its executives -- former Chief Executive Robert Kuzara, Chairman Carroll Lowenstein, director Michael Appe and Chief Financial Officer Carole Ouellette.
Also named were underwriters Coburn & Meredith Inc of Hartford and Media, Pa.-based Shamrock Partners Inc, which co-led the WebSecure public offering.
